neighbours.label: a lucky or welcome circumstance (It's a good thing ..., thanks to ..., just as well, fortunately), as opposed to the same words in plain senses
fire: It's a good thing I saved the receipt.
It's a good thing this plan has no chance.
Fortunately the neighbors never heard us.
They left early, which is just as well for us.
The kids can thrive, thanks to great teachers.
Luckily the bus was late that morning.
Thankfully the storm missed the town.
Good thing you brought an umbrella.
quiet: It's a good movie and I saved the ticket.
It's a bad thing that plan has no money.
The neighbors live on the other side of us.
They left early and got home by noon.
The kids can sing, and the teachers clap.
The bus was late that morning.
The storm hit the town at night.
A good umbrella costs ten dollars.

notes: 'Thankfully, the rain stopped' reached 0.24 in a probe with the peak on ' before', so the peak may not be the word.
